case_name: Uma Charan Roy vs Sm. Kajal Roy
facts_of_case: Appellant married Durga Bala in 1947 and Susama in 1959. He filed for divorce from Susama in 1963. Before the divorce was granted, he married Kajal in 1964. Kajal filed a suit claiming her marriage to the appellant was void as his marriage with Susama continued until their marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The term 'spouse' in Clause (a) of Section 4 would apply to a spouse married under the Hindu Marriage Act as well.
legal_principles.held: We cannot read into this section something which is not there. Moreover, if we accept this interpretation it would lead to disastrous results.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Marriage Act — Clause (a) of Section 4

legal_principles.principle: A party to a marriage cannot re-marry within at least one year since the date of the decree of dissolution of marriage.
legal_principles.held: It is clear from this section that at least for a year since the date of the decree of dissolution of marriage, a party to the marriage cannot re-marry, and if he or she remarries such a marriage shall be illegal.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decree of nullity of the marriage between the parties was upheld.
